sections_evaluated.name: Microsoft Defender
violations: CIS 2.1.10: no DMARC record published for domain 'contoso.com' -- SPF and DKIM failures have no enforcement disposition
CIS 2.1.11: malware filter policy 'Default' filters 2 file types; comprehensive attachment filtering expects at least 100
CIS 2.1.12: connection filter policy 'Default' uses an IP allow list, which bypasses spam and phishing evaluation for those senders
CIS 2.1.13: connection filter policy 'Default' has the safe list on, which trusts a third-party sender list wholesale
CIS 2.1.14: inbound anti-spam policy 'Default' contains allowed sender domains; a spoofed sender in an allowed domain is delivered unfiltered
CIS 2.1.15: outbound spam policy 'Default' has no external recipient-per-hour limit, so a compromised mailbox can send without a throttle
CIS 2.1.1: Safe Links policy 'Built-In Protection Policy' does not enable Safe Links for Office applications, so links in documents are not rewritten or checked at click time
CIS 2.1.2: malware filter policy 'Default' has the common attachment types filter disabled, so executable attachment types are not blocked by type
CIS 2.1.3: malware filter policy 'Default' does not send notifications for internal users sending malware, so a compromised internal mailbox goes unnoticed
CIS 2.1.4: Safe Attachments policy 'Built-In Protection Policy' exists but is not enabled
CIS 2.1.6: Exchange Online spam policy 'Default' is not set to notify administrators when outbound spam is detected
CIS 2.1.7: anti-phishing policy 'Office365 AntiPhish Default' has been created but is not enabled
CIS 2.1.8: no SPF record published for domain 'contoso.com' -- receivers cannot distinguish legitimate senders from spoofed mail
CIS 2.1.9: DKIM not enabled for domain 'contoso.com' -- outbound mail carries no cryptographic origin signature
CIS 2.4.1: no alert policy monitors priority accounts for detected malware in email -- a high-severity, inbound, priority-tagged alert with a notification recipient is required
CIS 2.4.1: no alert policy monitors priority accounts for phishing email detected at delivery -- a high-severity, inbound, priority-tagged alert with a notification recipient is required

sections_evaluated.name: Microsoft Entra admin center

unavailable_facts.pim_approval_62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012: no roleManagementPolicyAssignment for the Global Administrator role -- PIM does not govern its activation (blocks 5.3.4)
unavailable_facts.pim_approval_e8611ab8-c189-46e8-94e1-602: no roleManagementPolicyAssignment for the Privileged Role Administrator role -- PIM does not govern its activation (blocks 5.3.5)

violations: CIS 5.1.4.1: the ability to join devices to Entra is not restricted -- every user may join a device, so an attacker with credentials can register one
CIS 5.1.4.4: local administrator assignment is not limited during Entra join -- the registering user becomes a local admin on the device
CIS 5.1.4.5: Local Administrator Password Solution is not enabled, so local administrator passwords are neither randomised nor rotated
CIS 5.1.5.3: password addition is not blocked for applications, so a secret can be added to an existing app registration
CIS 5.1.5.4: no password lifetime restriction is enforced for applications, so an application password can exceed 180 days
CIS 5.1.5.5: new application passwords are not required to be system-generated, so a weak secret can be supplied by hand
CIS 5.1.5.6: no maximum certificate lifetime is enforced for applications, so an application certificate can exceed 180 days
CIS 5.1.6.1: no B2B collaboration domain policy exists, so invitations can be sent to any domain
CIS 5.1.6.2: guest user access is not restricted -- guest role is 'null' rather than the most restrictive role, so guests can enumerate directory objects
CIS 5.1.6.3: guest user invitations are not limited -- allowInvitesFrom is 'null', so ordinary members can invite external guests
CIS 5.2.2.10: no enabled Conditional Access policy requires a managed device to register security information, so an attacker can enrol their own MFA method
CIS 5.2.2.11: sign-in frequency for Intune enrollment is not set to every time
CIS 5.2.2.12: the device code sign-in flow is not blocked; it is a common phishing vector because the victim authenticates on their own device
CIS 5.2.2.13: periodic reauthentication is not required for all users -- no enabled policy sets a sign-in frequency
CIS 5.2.2.14: no trusted named locations are defined, so location cannot be used as a signal in Conditional Access
CIS 5.2.2.15: no exclusionary geographic access controls are utilized -- no country or region named location is defined
CIS 5.2.2.16: token protection is not enforced for session tokens, so a stolen refresh token can be replayed from another device
CIS 5.2.2.17: authentication transfer is not blocked, so a session can be handed from a desktop to an attacker-controlled device
CIS 5.2.2.1: no enabled Conditional Access policy requires multifactor authentication for administrative roles
CIS 5.2.2.2: no enabled Conditional Access policy requires multifactor authentication for all users
CIS 5.2.2.3: no enabled Conditional Access policy blocks legacy authentication; legacy protocols bypass multifactor authentication
CIS 5.2.2.4: no enabled Conditional Access policy sets a sign-in frequency with browser sessions made non-persistent, so a stolen session cookie stays valid indefinitely
CIS 5.2.2.5: phishing-resistant MFA strength is not required for administrators; a policy requiring generic MFA still admits phishable factors
CIS 5.2.2.6: no enabled Identity Protection user risk policy exists, so a user flagged as compromised is not challenged or blocked
CIS 5.2.2.7: no enabled Identity Protection sign-in risk policy exists, so a risky sign-in is not challenged
CIS 5.2.2.8: sign-in risk is not blocked for both medium and high risk levels
CIS 5.2.2.9: no enabled Conditional Access policy requires a managed device for authentication
CIS 5.2.3.10: Microsoft Authenticator on companion applications is not disabled, which widens the surface on which an approval can be granted
CIS 5.2.3.1: Microsoft Authenticator is not configured to protect against MFA fatigue -- 'show_app_information_state' is not enabled, so a push can be approved without seeing what is being approved

CIS 5.2.3.1: Microsoft Authenticator is not configured to protect against MFA fatigue -- 'show_geographic_location_state' is not enabled, so a push can be approved without seeing what is being approved
CIS 5.2.3.2: no custom banned passwords list is configured; the global list does not cover organization-specific terms
CIS 5.2.3.3: password protection is not enabled for on-prem Active Directory, so weak passwords set on-premises are never evaluated
CIS 5.2.3.5: weak authentication method 'sms' is enabled; SMS and voice are phishable and interceptable
CIS 5.2.3.5: weak authentication method 'voice' is enabled; SMS and voice are phishable and interceptable
CIS 5.2.3.7: the email OTP authentication method is enabled; a mailbox compromise then satisfies the second factor
CIS 5.3.1: Privileged Identity Management is not in use; privileged role assignments are standing rather than activated on demand
CIS 5.3.2: no access review is configured for guest users, so external access is never re-attested
CIS 5.3.3: no access review is configured for privileged roles, so standing administrative access is never re-attested
CIS 5.3.4: could not be evaluated -- no roleManagementPolicyAssignment for the Global Administrator role -- PIM does not govern its activation (blocks 5.3.4) (this is not a pass)
CIS 5.3.5: could not be evaluated -- no roleManagementPolicyAssignment for the Privileged Role Administrator role -- PIM does not govern its activation (blocks 5.3.5) (this is not a pass)

sections_evaluated.name: Exchange admin center
violations: CIS 6.1.3: AuditBypassEnabled is set on 'svc-backup', so actions against that mailbox are excluded from the audit record
CIS 6.2.1: outbound spam policy 'Default' has AutoForwardingMode 'On'; automatic mail forwarding to external recipients should be blocked
CIS 6.2.1: transport rule 'Allow partner' redirects mail to another recipient, which is a form of forwarding the benchmark requires be blocked
CIS 6.2.2: transport rule 'Allow partner' whitelists specific sender domains by bypassing spam filtering (SCL -1); a spoofed sender in that domain is delivered unfiltered
CIS 6.2.3: email from external senders is not identified in Outlook, removing the visual cue users rely on to spot impersonation
CIS 6.3.1: role assignment policy 'Default Role Assignment Policy' grants 'My Custom Apps', which allows users installing Outlook add-ins
CIS 6.3.1: role assignment policy 'Default Role Assignment Policy' grants 'My Marketplace Apps', which allows users installing Outlook add-ins
CIS 6.3.2: OWA mailbox policy 'OwaMailboxPolicy-Default' permits adding personal accounts and third-party storage in Outlook on the web
CIS 6.5.3: OWA mailbox policy 'OwaMailboxPolicy-Default' leaves additional storage providers available in Outlook on the web, so attachments can be saved to third-party storage

evidence_strength.section: collected with Get-PnPTenant, not the Get-SPOTenant the benchmark documents -- Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell is Windows-only and cannot run in a Linux execution environment. The same CSOM tenant properties are read.

sections_evaluated.name: SharePoint admin center
violations: CIS 7.2.1: SharePoint tenant facts were not collected, so whether modern authentication is required could not be established -- section 7 was not evaluated (this is not a pass)

evidence_strength.section: collected with the cmdlets CIS documents (Get-CsTeamsClientConfiguration, Get-CsTenantFederationConfiguration, Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, Get-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy), all verified present in the execution environment. Meeting and messaging policies are evaluated across ALL policies, not only Global, because a permissive non-global policy still governs the users it is assigned to.

sections_evaluated.name: Microsoft Teams admin center
violations: CIS 8.5.8: meeting policy 'Global' leaves external meeting chat on

evidence_strength.section: collected from the Fabric admin API. CIS documents these as portal steps plus a CIS-supplied helper function; the API returns the same tenantSettings the portal displays. A setting that is enabled but scoped to named security groups is treated as restricted, which is what the benchmark accepts.
